data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"An append-only event log actually requires a property stronger than RFC 9110 idempotence: it requires write-ordered idempotence, where not only must duplicate writes be suppressed, but the ordering of non-duplicate writes must be preserved. RFC 9110 idempotence is order-insensitive (PUT A then PUT A then PUT B yields the same state as PUT A then PUT B). But an event log with at-least-once delivery needs order-preserving deduplication: event A, event B, retry of event A must yield [A, B], not [A, B, A]. This ordering constraint is absent from RFC 9110's definition and represents a strictly stronger requirement.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the event log is defined as unordered (a set of events rather than a sequence), the ordering constraint disappears and standard idempotence suffices","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If RFC 9110's idempotence definition is interpreted broadly enough to cover ordering invariants (which it likely is not, being defined for individual HTTP methods), the 'stronger than idempotence' claim fails","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"RFC 9110 idempotence for PUT says N identical requests yield the same final state as 1 \u2014 it says nothing about interleaving with other requests. In an event log, events are ordered, and a retry of an earlier event arriving after later events have been appended must not produce a duplicate in the wrong position. This requires the log to track which logical events have already been appended (e.g., by sequence number) and suppress late-arriving retries, preserving the original order. This is deduplication with ordering, a compound property not captured by either 'safe' or 'idempotent' alone.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
